response: As I sit here on my [birthday] alone, I'm struck by the realization that I've spent most of my life carrying the weight of family expectations on my own shoulders. Growing up as an only child, I never had to navigate the complexities of sibling relationships or share the burden of household responsibilities with anyone else. (This has led to a unique dynamic where I've had to rely heavily on myself to get things done, and it's a skill that's served me well in many areas of my life.) But as I've grown older, I've come to understand that this self-reliance has also meant that I've had to shoulder the weight of family expectations alone. (It's a heavy burden, and one that I've often felt like I'm carrying in silence.) Quiet dinners with my parents have been a space for me to process these feelings, and to gain a deeper understanding of the ways in which my upbringing has shaped my approach to life's challenges and relationships. (For example, I've learned to be more independent and self-sufficient, but I've also struggled with feelings of loneliness and disconnection.) As I look back on my life, I'm starting to realize that being an only child has given me a unique perspective on solitude and family dynamics. (It's a perspective that's both a blessing and a curse, and one that I'm still grappling with as I navigate the complexities of adulthood.)
